Kenichi Takahashi (高橋 健一, *Takahashi Ken'ichi*) is a former Japanese professional basketball player and coach who made significant contributions to Japanese basketball, particularly in the **Japan Basketball League (JBL)** and later the **B.League**. Here’s everything I could gather about him:

---

### **1. Playing Career**
#### **High School & College**
- **High School**: Played for **Nara Ikuei High School** (奈良育英高校), a powerhouse in Japanese high school basketball.
- **College**: Attended **Nippon Sport Science University (NSSU, 日本体育大学)**, a well-known basketball program in Japan.

#### **Professional Career**
- **Toyota Motors / Alvark Tokyo (1990s–2000s)**
  - Takahashi joined **Toyota Motors** (later renamed **Toyota Alvark**, now **Alvark Tokyo**) in the **Japan Basketball League (JBL)**.
  - Played as a **forward/center**, known for his **defensive skills, rebounding, and leadership**.
  - Helped Toyota win multiple **JBL championships** in the 1990s and early 2000s.
  - Was part of the team’s golden era alongside players like **Takehiko Orimo** and **Satoru Furuta**.

- **Retirement**
  - Retired as a player in **2005** after a long career with Toyota.

---

### **2. Coaching Career**
After retiring, Takahashi transitioned into coaching, where he had a major impact on Japanese basketball.

#### **Toyota Alvark / Alvark Tokyo (2005–2016)**
- **Assistant Coach (2005–2010)**
  - Worked under head coaches like **Toru Suzuki** and **Kazuo Nakamura**.
  - Helped develop young players and refine the team’s system.

- **Head Coach (2010–2016)**
  - Took over as head coach in **2010** and led the team to:
    - **JBL Championship (2011–12 season)**
    - **NBL (National Basketball League) Championship (2015–16 season)**
  - Known for his **defensive-minded coaching style**, emphasizing **teamwork and discipline**.
  - Coached future Japanese national team players like **Yuta Watanabe** (before he went to the NBA) and **Daiki Tanaka**.
  - Left Alvark Tokyo in **2016** after the team’s transition to the **B.League**.

#### **Japan National Team (2016–2019)**
- **Assistant Coach (2016–2019)**
  - Served under head coach **Julio Lamas** (Argentina) during the **2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup** qualification cycle.
  - Helped Japan secure a **spot in the 2019 World Cup** (held in China).
  - Worked closely with NBA players **Rui Hachimura** and **Yuta Watanabe** during their early national team days.

#### **Shiga Lakes (2019–2021)**
- **Head Coach (2019–2021)**
  - Joined **Shiga Lakes** (now **Shiga Lakes Basketball Club**) in the **B.League** (B2 division).
  - Aimed to rebuild the team but left in **2021** due to mixed results.

#### **Return to Alvark Tokyo (2021–2023)**
- **Assistant Coach (2021–2023)**
  - Rejoined Alvark Tokyo under head coach **Luca Banchi** (former assistant for the Dallas Mavericks).
  - Helped the team reach the **B.League Finals in 2023** (lost to Chiba Jets).
  - Left the team after the **2022–23 season**.

#### **Current Status (2024)**
- As of 2024, Takahashi is **not actively coaching** in the B.League or national team.
- He remains a respected figure in Japanese basketball and occasionally appears in **media and basketball clinics**.

---

### **3. Playing Style & Legacy**
- **As a Player**:
  - A **defensive specialist**, known for **tough rebounding and physical play**.
  - Not a high-volume scorer but a **glue guy** who elevated team defense.
  - Played a key role in Toyota’s dominance in the JBL.

- **As a Coach**:
  - **Defensive mastermind** – his teams were known for **tight defense and structured play**.
  - **Player development** – helped nurture young Japanese talent (e.g., Yuta Watanabe).
  - **Adaptability** – transitioned well from the JBL to the NBL and later the B.League.
  - **International experience** – worked with foreign coaches (e.g., Julio Lamas) and adapted modern basketball strategies.

---

### **4. Personal Life & Other Roles**
- **Media Appearances**:
  - Occasionally appears as a **basketball analyst** on Japanese sports networks (e.g., **NHK, J Sports**).
  - Provides commentary on **B.League games** and **Japanese national team performances**.

- **Mentorship**:
  - Known for mentoring young coaches in Japan.
  - Has been involved in **basketball clinics** for youth players.

- **Family**:
  - Not much public information, but he is known to be **private about his personal life**.

---

### **5. Achievements & Honors**
#### **As a Player**
- **Multiple JBL Championships** (with Toyota Motors/Alvark)
- **JBL Best Five (All-Japan Team)** – Multiple selections
- **JBL Rebounding Leader** (at least once)

#### **As a Coach**
- **JBL Championship (2011–12)** – Toyota Alvark
- **NBL Championship (2015–16)** – Toyota Alvark
- **B.League Finals Appearance (2023)** – Alvark Tokyo
- **FIBA World Cup Qualification (2019)** – Japan National Team

---

### **6. Influence on Japanese Basketball**
- **Bridged the gap** between the old JBL/NBL era and the modern B.League.
- **Helped develop NBA-level talent** (e.g., Yuta Watanabe, Rui Hachimura).
- **Advocated for defensive play**, which has become a hallmark of Japanese basketball.
- **Respected by peers** for his **work ethic, basketball IQ, and leadership**.

---

### **7. Where to Follow Him**
- **Twitter/X**: [@kenichi_takahashi](https://twitter.com/) (if active, but he is not very active on social media).
- **B.League Website**: [https://www.bleague.jp](https://www.bleague.jp) (for past coaching stats).
- **Japanese Basketball Media**:
  - **Basket Count** (バスケットカウント) – [https://www.basket-count.com](https://www.basket-count.com)
  - **NHK Sports** – [https://www.nhk.or.jp/sports](https://www.nhk.or.jp/sports)

---

### **8. Fun Facts**
- Nicknamed **"Taka-san"** by players and fans.
- Known for his **calm demeanor** on the sidelines, even in high-pressure games.
- One of the few Japanese coaches with **extensive experience in both domestic and international basketball**.
- Played in an era when Japanese basketball was **less globalized**, making his transition to coaching in the B.League era impressive.

---

### **9. Comparison to Other Japanese Coaches**
| Coach | Style | Notable Achievements |
|--------|--------|----------------------|
| **Kenichi Takahashi** | Defensive, structured, player development | JBL/NBL titles, B.League Finals, World Cup qualification |
| **Yuta Nakamura** (Chiba Jets) | Fast-paced, offensive | Multiple B.League titles, developed NBA players |
| **Toru Suzuki** (Former Alvark coach) | Balanced, veteran leadership | JBL titles, mentored Takahashi |
| **Julio Lamas** (Former Japan NT coach) | International experience | World Cup qualification, worked with Takahashi |

Takahashi is often seen as a **defensive counterpart** to more offensive-minded coaches like Yuta Nakamura.

---

### **10. Future Prospects**
- Could return to coaching in the **B.League or national team** if an opportunity arises.
- Might take on a **consulting or advisory role** for Japanese basketball development.
- Could become a **full-time basketball analyst** if he steps away from coaching.

---

### **Final Thoughts**
Kenichi Takahashi is one of the most **understated yet influential figures** in modern Japanese basketball. While he may not be as flashy as some of today’s B.League coaches, his **defensive acumen, leadership, and ability to develop players** have left a lasting impact. His career reflects the **evolution of Japanese basketball** from the JBL era to the globalized B.League.
